issue_context.title: Rendering issue with some objects on Chrome
issue_context.body:
Attach (recommended) or Link to PDF file here:
[Test file.pdf](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/files/4656226/Test.file.pdf)

Configuration:
- Web browser and its version: Chrome Version 81.0.4044.138 (Official Build) (64-bit)
- Operating system and its version: Windows 10
- PDF.js version: latest
- Is a browser extension: no

Steps to reproduce the problem:
1. Open [https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html](https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/web/viewer.html)
2. Load the provided .pdf file

What is the expected behavior? (add screenshot)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5569382/82438616-02c3fe80-9aa2-11ea-9003-b75ea1e7aac6.png)

What went wrong? (add screenshot)
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/5569382/82438640-09527600-9aa2-11ea-810b-071da7e37896.png)
comments: This looks like a Chrome-specific rendering bug since the file is rendered properly in Firefox 76.0.1 for me.
Looks OK in Google Chrome 88 now, probably fixed by either PR #12812 and/or #12864.

The bug is still there: it depends of the zoom level.
I filed a bug on chrome's side: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=1170396

review_comments: Should we mention here that this constant can be removed entirely once the upstream bug is fixed? Or should this patch basically be reverted in that case, given that the 1.000001 number was already in use before this patch if `absDet > Number.EPSILON`?
In the updated patch the multiplication by the constant is chrome-only.
